strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph structural ordering
Replacement scope: Replace the construction phase inside `get_best_schedule` — the initial permutation is no longer built by greedy simulation from a random start, but derived from the workload's conflict structure (keys shared between transactions), then locally improved.
Compute budget: Build the conflict graph once per workload (O(n²·ops) ≈ negligible). Spend ≤105s per workload on improvement restarts seeded from the structural orderings; keep the existing deadline guard and always return a complete permutation.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent greedy only sees incremental cost and is blind to global conflict structure: transactions sharing many hot keys should be adjacent so their conflicting operations resolve with minimal delay. New degree of freedom: an explicit weighted conflict graph where edge weight = number of shared keys (write-write weighted higher), used to (a) order transactions by a degree/weight heuristic (e.g., highest total conflict weight first, breaking ties by number of writes), and (b) run a nearest-neighbor construction that appends the transaction with maximum conflict weight against the already-placed set (a max-conflict-adjacency tour, analogous to a TSP tour on the conflict graph), with several tie-breaking variants as distinct seeds. These complete permutations are then evaluated with `get_opt_seq_cost` and the best kept; optionally refine the top few with the incumbent's greedy-append local search. Validity is preserved because every construction yields a full permutation of range(n), and the caller recomputes true cost. Falsifiable threshold: if the best conflict-graph tour beats the incumbent greedy on any workload's makespan, the mechanism is validated; expected gain check: the incumbent cannot exploit conflict adjacency at all, so if max-adjacency tours reduce total makespan below the current 297 sum, combined_score strictly exceeds 3355.7.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: local search over full permutations (structural, not parameter polish)
Replacement scope: Replace the multi-restart greedy construction loop in `get_best_schedule` with a local search over complete schedules: start from a few greedy-built permutations (reuse the incumbent greedy as a seed generator, ~5 restarts), then iteratively apply improvement moves evaluated with the true `get_opt_seq_cost`.
Compute budget: ≤105s per workload; each move evaluation is one simulator call; cap restarts at 5 and stop any restart at the deadline, always returning the best complete permutation found so far.
Gain mechanism: New degrees of freedom the greedy lacks: (1) relocation moves — remove one transaction and reinsert it at every other position, accepting the first or best improvement; (2) adjacent-pair and random swap moves; (3) 2-opt-like segment reversal on the permutation. The greedy is myopic and never revisits earlier placements; local search on the complete permutation can escape poor early choices (e.g., a hot-key transaction placed too early that delays many successors). Each accepted move strictly decreases true makespan, so monotone improvement is guaranteed; validity holds because all moves preserve permutation completeness. Falsifiable threshold: if relocation/swap local search starting from incumbent greedy seeds yields any workload cost below the incumbent's, the mechanism works; expected gain check: the incumbent has no mechanism to correct an early bad placement, so any strictly lower total makespan than 297 implies combined_score > 3355.7.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam search construction (global lookahead, different construction mechanism)
Replacement scope: Replace the single-path greedy construction entirely: instead of committing to one transaction per step, maintain B partial schedules (beam) of equal length, expand each with the top-k cheapest next transactions by `get_opt_seq_cost`, prune back to B best partials, and finalize the best complete schedule; optionally polish it with a short local-search phase.
Compute budget: B=8–16, k=3–5 expansions per beam node per step; cost is B·k·n simulator calls per construction (~thousands for n=100), so budget ~2–3 beam runs per workload within 105s, with deadline checks between steps and a greedy fallback permutation if time runs out mid-beam.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent greedy is a width-1 search: a single locally-cheapest choice can force large conflicts later (the classic greedy trap when the cheapest append consumes a hot key that many remaining transactions need). Beam search keeps multiple competing prefixes alive, so it can avoid committing to a prefix that is cheap now but expensive to complete — a degree of freedom (search width with lookahead pruning) the incumbent structurally lacks. Validity: every beam element is a partial permutation; completion yields a full permutation of range(n), and the final result is verified by recomputing with `get_opt_seq_cost` in the caller. Falsifiable threshold: if any beam run completes with total makespan below the incumbent's per-workload costs, the trap-avoidance hypothesis is confirmed; expected gain check: the incumbent width-1 construction cannot recover from a bad prefix, so any beam-produced total makespan < 297 yields combined_score > 3355.7.

strategies.title: [conflict-graph-clustering] Block-based construction from conflict-graph communi
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph structural decomposition (mesoscopic subsystem ordering)
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction phase inside `get_best_schedule` (the beam + greedy completion block); keep the descent/restart local search as polish.
Compute budget: Graph build is O(n²) key scans once per workload; spectral/community clustering on ≤100 nodes is negligible. Same 100s per-workload deadline; the freed beam budget goes to more restarts.
Gain mechanism: Transactions sharing hot keys form dense conflict clusters; makespan is dominated by how these clusters are interleaved. The incumbent's beam builds the permutation one transaction at a time and cannot see that a whole *group* of mutually-conflicting transactions should be contiguous. Build an undirected weighted graph (weight = number of shared keys, read-write and write-write both counting), partition into communities via a simple greedy modularity/agglomerative merge (e.g., union-find merging the pair of clusters with largest shared-key weight, cap cluster count at ~√n), then order clusters by a greedy cluster-level beam (cost = true `get_opt_seq_cost` of a representative concatenation), and order transactions within each cluster by the existing descent. Concatenate cluster orders to form the seed permutation. Invariant: output is always a permutation of range(n); identity fallback preserved.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is contiguous placement of conflict-dense transaction groups, which neither the element-wise beam nor relocation/swap/2-opt moves can reach without many coordinated moves; falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below the incumbent's 244 (combined_score > 4081.63).

strategies.title: [or-opt-insertion-descent] Segment-based Or-opt moves with simulated-annealing a
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: local search over full permutations with segment (Or-opt) move family and non-monotone acceptance
Replacement scope: Replace the `descend` function and the double-bridge restart loop's acceptance rule inside `get_best_schedule`.
Compute budget: Same 100s deadline; Or-opt evaluates 3 segment lengths × O(n²) positions per pass, comparable to current relocation cost; annealing adds no new cost evaluations beyond existing moves.
Gain mechanism: The current descent accepts only strict improvements, so it gets trapped in local minima that a single-element relocation cannot escape, and double-bridge restarts discard descent progress when they fail. Add Or-opt moves (move segments of length 1–3 to another position, both orientations) — these move *co-dependent* transactions together, which single-element relocation breaks apart — and replace strict-improvement acceptance with late-acceptance/annealing: keep a cycling list of the last L=8 incumbent costs, accept a candidate if it beats the worst entry in that list. This lets the search cross small cost barriers that strict descent cannot, without the random-destructive nature of double-bridge. Keep best-ever solution separately; identity fallback and permutation invariant unchanged.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is joint relocation of small co-conflicting segments plus barrier-crossing acceptance, unreachable by the incumbent's strict-improvement single-element moves; falsifiable threshold: makespan ≤ 240 (combined_score ≥ ~4149) on the three-workload evaluation.

strategies.title: [lin-kernighan-style] Ejection-chain / compound-move search on the permutation
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: compound ejection-chain local search (structural exploration of permutation space)
Replacement scope: Replace the entire search pipeline inside `get_best_schedule` (beam seed, descent, restarts) with: greedy nearest-neighbor seed by true prefix cost, then an ejection-chain (Lin–Kernighan-style) search until deadline; keep identity fallback.
Compute budget: One chain pass is O(n²) cost evaluations (same order as one current descent sweep); run chains repeatedly within the same 100s per-workload deadline, chain depth capped at n.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent evaluates each candidate move independently and resets after each accepted move; an ejection chain builds a compound move by sequentially relocating elements, tentatively tracking the best partial chain cost along the way, and commits only the best prefix of the chain. This reaches permutations that are k relocations away (k up to ~n) in a single compound move — a direction none of the incumbent's independent 1-move families (relocation, swap, 2-opt) or random double-bridge can traverse deterministically. Implementation: start chain at position i, repeatedly remove the element that most reduces tentative cost when reinserted elsewhere, record running cost after each chain step, stop when no improving insertion exists or depth cap; revert to the best recorded prefix and repeat from the next i. All candidates evaluated with true `get_opt_seq_cost` (cached); output always a full permutation; identity fallback if deadline hits before first chain completes.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is deterministic multi-relocation compound moves, which the incumbent's single-move strict-improvement descent structurally cannot execute; falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below 244, i.e. combined_score > 4081.63 on the unchanged evaluator.

strategies.title: [ruin-and-recreate] Iterated partial destruction and greedy reconstruction of tr
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ruin-and-recreate (LNS-style block reinsertion)
Replacement scope: Replace the double-bridge restart loop and `descend` in `get_best_schedule` (keep beam seed and cost cache).
Compute budget: ~100s per workload deadline (unchanged); each ruin-recreate cycle removes a block of 10–25 transactions, reinserts greedily by true prefix cost — O(k·n) simulator calls per cycle, thousands of cycles fit in budget.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's escape move (double-bridge) is a fixed four-cut reassembly that only permutes whole segments; it cannot discover that a cluster of transactions on the same hot keys belongs interleaved with others. Removing a contiguous/conflict-linked block and reinserting each transaction at its true-best position (best-of-all-positions insertion, evaluated with `get_opt_seq_cost`) is a compound move no combination of relocation/swap/2-opt first-improvement steps can reach monotonically — the incumbent's descent is strictly monotone, so it is trapped in local optima that require temporarily worsening intermediate states. Ruin selection alternates between (a) random contiguous windows and (b) blocks formed by taking a seed transaction plus all transactions sharing a written key with it (extracted via `workload.get_txn_ops` with defensive try/except over attribute names, falling back to random blocks if unavailable). Keep identity permutation fallback and accept only strict improvements to the incumbent; cache costs by tuple key. Validity preserved because every candidate is a full permutation of `range(n)`, asserted before return.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is best-position reinsertion of a conflict-linked block, which the monotone 2-opt/swap/relocation descent provably cannot reach; falsifiable threshold: total makespan (currently 244) must drop, i.e., combined_score must exceed 4081.63.

strategies.title: [conflict-dag-layering] Topological layer decomposition with per-layer exhaustiv
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-DAG layering
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction phase (keep the local-search polish and restart loop as polish on top).
Compute budget: DAG build is O(total ops) once; layer ordering uses beam/greedy with true cost within layers only; overall stays within the 100s/workload deadline; polish budget reduced to ~60s to make room.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent builds the permutation purely by prefix-cost beam search, which is myopic: it never uses the structure of read/write conflicts. Build the conflict graph between transactions (edge if they share a written key, or a write/read on the same key), compute a topological-style layer decomposition (layer = transactions whose predecessors are all in earlier layers, e.g., by longest-path depth in the DAG of a reference order). Then schedule layer by layer, but within each layer search orderings by true simulator cost — transactions in the same layer are conflict-light, so their relative order is exactly where the beam search wastes lookahead. This changes the optimized subsystem: instead of searching the whole permutation space with a greedy prefix heuristic, it fixes the macroscopic conflict-imposed skeleton and optimizes only the free (intra-layer) orderings, a mesoscopic decomposition the incumbent lacks. Seed the existing descent with the result; keep identity fallback and accept only improvements. Validity: every candidate is a complete permutation of all n transactions; DAG is only used to guide ordering, never to drop or duplicate transactions, so any ordering is feasible.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the conflict-layer skeleton that decouples macroscopic ordering from free intra-layer ordering, which prefix-greedy beam search cannot represent; falsifiable threshold: combined_score must exceed the incumbent's 4081.63 on the three-workload evaluation.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: population memetic crossover (OX over elite pool)
Replacement scope: Replace the single-incumbent restart loop with a population of P≈8 schedules maintained and recombined (descend kept as mutation/polish).
Compute budget: population of 8, one OX crossover + short capped descent (≤50 improvement evaluations per offspring) per iteration until the 100s/workload deadline; cost cache shared.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent explores via perturbation of one solution (a single trajectory); all its restarts are double-bridge kicks of the same incumbent, so search diversity collapses quickly. A population of schedules from different beam seeds (and the identity order) recombined by order crossover (OX) — take a random slice from parent A, fill remaining positions in parent B's relative order — produces offspring that inherit large coherent ordering blocks from two distinct good solutions, a recombination move unreachable by any single-trajectory perturbation. Selection: replace the worst if the offspring beats it; occasional immigration via double-bridge on a random elite to maintain diversity. Each offspring gets a short capped descent so the population converges memetically without blowing the budget. Keep identity fallback, tuple-key cost cache, and return the best individual; every candidate is a complete permutation (OX guarantees a permutation), asserted before return.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is recombination of coherent blocks from two distinct good schedules, which the single-trajectory double-bridge incumbent cannot generate; falsifiable threshold: combined_score must exceed 4081.63, else the diversity hypothesis is refuted.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tabu-memory-descent
Replacement scope: Replace the ruin-and-recreate main loop (the `while time.time() < deadline` block and `stall_count` logic) while keeping the beam seed, `cost` cache, and `best_seq/best_cost` fallback.
Compute budget: Hard deadline unchanged (~100s per workload, total ≤360s). strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: critical-key-group-exhaustive
Replacement scope: Replace the beam construction and greedy completion (from `# Beam construction` through the seed-tracking loop) with a subsystem decomposition; keep the incumbent's ruin-and-recreate/reversal polish loop unchanged as a post-pass.
Compute budget: ~15s decomposition + exhaustive group packing, remainder (~80s) inherited by the existing polish loop; groups capped at 8 transactions so each subproblem is ≤8! ≈ 40320 permutations evaluated once against the simulator (cached); overall well inside the per-workload 100s and 360s total.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's beam and ruin moves treat all transactions symmetrically, but makespan is dominated by long read/write conflict chains on a few hot keys. Grouping all transactions that touch a given hot key and optimally ordering that group (by trying all permutations of the group with the rest fixed, or DP over group order interleaved greedily) directly attacks the chains the beam can only order greedily.
